I've been farming this land for over 40 years. My husband passed, my children are in the city, and I manage my 5 mu mostly on my own, with help from neighbors during harvest. I don't read much, but I know this land. I watch what my neighbors do and I listen to the seed dealer in town.

**My thinking:**

Everyone here in Quzhou grows wheat in winter and maize in summer. That's what the land is for. That's what the grain stations buy. I'm not going to try cotton or peanuts — I don't know those crops and the buyers aren't nearby. Wheat and maize, same as always.

For seeds, I buy from the township dealer. I stopped saving my own wheat seed a long time ago because the dealer's improved variety gives more grain. For maize, he sells hybrid seeds — everyone uses those now, they're taller and fill out better.

For fertilizer, I put down diammonium phosphate and urea at planting, and add more urea when the wheat is jointing. My neighbor uses the same amount and gets good harvests, so I follow that. I probably use a bit more than I need to — I'd rather not risk a thin harvest.

Water is the problem here. I pay for the pumped groundwater. I'll water wheat three times: once in winter to protect the roots, once when it starts jointing, once when it's filling grain. For maize, I'll water twice if there's no rain by August — usually during silking.

For maize I don't plow. I just direct-seed into the wheat stubble. Saves me work and the soil stays better. For wheat I'll do rotary tillage to chop up the maize stalks.

Pesticides — I spray herbicide on wheat in early spring when the weeds come up, and spray once more for powdery mildew before heading. For maize I spray once for armyworm if I see it, which I usually do.
